track: Capture-based photorealism for a walkable Aokigahara on an M2 Air: Gaussian splats, photogrammetry and hybrids in 2026
summary:
Photographic only in small, fixed places, and not on the recommended Godot path. A 2026 splat of Aokigahara's trails would look photographic for moss, lava, roots and trunks within a few metres of the walked line, in the light and wind of the capture day.

- **Off the path:** quality falls away; street-scene FID roughly quadruples by a 5 m sideways shift.
- **Vegetation:** the weakest case even on held-out views, about 5 dB PSNR below indoor scenes. Twigs, needles and sky gaps smear.
- **Lighting:** captured splats cannot take the world's sun. Apple RealityKit, PlayCanvas and Godot GDGS all document that splats do not receive shadows. Relighting is proxy modulation or offline CUDA research.
- **Runtime:** streaming at trail length exists in PlayCanvas and Spark, not in Godot. GDGS has no LOD, and its one Mac report showed Metal shader failures.
- **M2 budget:** 1–3 M splats is plausible but unmeasured.
- **Coverage:** the repo's OSM data has about 9 km of named trail in the best 5 × 5 km lava window, and 40 km of paths in all. Photographic corridors would cover about 1% of the plot, 3% at most.
- **MMS roads:** colour-true points, not photographs, near the camera.

In free roam the seams would break the illusion. Captures fit best as a separate trail-walk mode, as calibration truth, and as photogrammetry for ground assets the engine can light.

None of the owner's 13 real photos passes the UE-derived lighting gate (warm highlights 0/13).

Housekeeping: I overwrote the scratch copy `refphotos/U01_c59f556b_1280.jpg` by mistake and rebuilt it from its WebP original.

findings.claim:
No walkable forest-trail splat was found.

- **Closest analogue:** SuperSplat's 'Mononoke Forest', the Shirakoma moss forest in Nagano. It is one spot, captured in 1,373 OM-1 Mark II photos, and can be explored in SuperSplat's walk mode.
- **Best large walkable captures are urban:** Vincent Woo's Grace Cathedral streams LOD within 400 m, rendering 3.5 M splats on desktop and 1.4 M on mobile. PlayCanvas's Lokwelt museum scene has 24 M splats at its top LOD.
- **Aokigahara:** no public splat or scan exists.

superspl.at is blocked by the proxy, so I could not judge these scenes by eye; the owner can open them on the Mac.

Vegetation is the hardest case even for held-out views taken along the capture path. gsplat's reproduced Mip-NeRF 360 results at 30k iterations:

| Scene | PSNR | SSIM | LPIPS |
|---|---|---|---|
| bicycle | 25.22 | 0.764 | 0.172 |
| stump (a forest-floor tree stump) | 26.53 | 0.768 | 0.153 |
| room | 31.36 | 0.918 | 0.164 |
| bonsai | 32.06 | 0.941 | 0.132 |

Quality collapses away from the walked line.

- **Sideways shift:** DriveSplat reports StreetGS FID of 38.3, 61.9 and 149.6 at 1, 2 and 5 m. Roads have planar priors; forests do not.
- **Wind:** even a light breeze leaves floaters.
- **Under the canopy:** SfM initialisation lacks points there, and 3DGS leaves parts unreconstructed.
- **Foliage:** gets a hull rather than a surface.
- **People:** passing walkers must be masked out.
- **Frozen foliage:** a splat has no wind, while synthetic trees beside it would sway.

I measured the owner's 13 real Aokigahara photos with `tools/lighting_stats.py`. None meets all four primary targets of the UE-derived lighting gate.

| Target | Photos passing | Photo range | Target range |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm highlights (B/R) | 0/13 | 0.59–0.80 | 0.29–0.42 |
| Black fraction | 2/13 | 0.06–0.22 | — |
| Exposure key | 5/13 | — | — |
| Sunfleck | 7/13 | — | — |

Sky peak passes in 12 of 13 and clipping in all 13.

A literally photographic capture would therefore fail the gate: the gate encodes the UE5.8 look, not reality. Caveats: the photos' camera and processing are unknown, and they are 1280×629 crops.

No 2026 renderer that runs on this Mac lets captured splats receive the scene's shadows.

- **Apple RealityKit** (GaussianSplatComponent, macOS 27.0): 'Scene lighting doesn't affect a Gaussian splat asset.' The only shadow is a spherical grounding shadow.
- **PlayCanvas:** splats cast shadows but 'cannot directly receive' them. The workaround is a shadow-catcher mesh.
- **GDGS 3.3.0 (Godot):** relighting only modulates the splats and 'cannot remove light that was baked in'. 'Splats do not receive cast shadows.' Foliage gets a hull. Lighting splats natively was measured at 2.5–3.9× the frame time.
- **Spark 2.2.0:** no shadow receiving. I inspected the npm tarball; its shader graph exposes shadow samplers, so it could be custom-built.
- **Omniverse RTX:** its particle fields do cast and receive shadows, but need NVIDIA RTX hardware.

The only workable hybrid is PlayCanvas's GsplatRelighting.

- **How it works:** a proxy mesh is lit with standard lights (PCSS sun, HDRI) into a screen-space texture, which multiplies each splat fragment.
- **Quality limit:** in PlayCanvas's words, 'proxy mesh quality directly drives the result'.
- **Applied to Aokigahara (my judgement):** with an overcast capture, synthetic canopy shadows could be laid over captured moss and lava. Fern fronds and twigs would get misplaced light, and baked sunflecks cannot be removed.
- **In Godot:** this would have to be written as a compositor effect.

Research relighting does not close the gap for forests.

- **ROS-GS** (TVCG 2026) separates sun and sky using 2DGS and ray-traced shadows, but masks sky and foliage out of the shadow computation.
- **GaRe** relights outdoor scenes built from photo collections.
- **LightBridge** (September 2026) re-bakes a whole 3DGS to new lighting in about 3.3 s. It runs offline and was tested on synthetic indoor scenes.

All three need CUDA, and none gives a dynamic sun with shadows on an M2.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11275 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20512 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02543 (read via search snippets; arXiv is proxy-blocked)

findings.claim:
Exposure is a second seam.

- **The glTF standard:** the ratified KHR_gaussian_splatting spec makes splats display-referred, so scene exposure and tonemapping do not apply to them.
- **PlayCanvas default:** splats go through the tone curve, exposure and fog.
- **Opting out:** the splats then clip and 'look inconsistent' next to tonemapped meshes. PlayCanvas advises adjusting the capture instead.
- **Camera clipping:** anything the camera clipped cannot be recovered.

Performance evidence for Apple GPUs:

| Source | Device | Resolution | Splats | Frame time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PlayCanvas benchmark (WebGPU) | M4 Max | 1298×962 | 1–4 M | 6.5–7.4 ms |
| PlayCanvas benchmark (WebGPU) | M4 Max | 1298×962 | 35 M | 13.2 ms (WebGL 2 is 5.7× slower) |
| PlayCanvas benchmark (WebGPU) | iPhone 13 Pro Max | 642×1126 | 1–4 M | 12.9–23.6 ms |
| WebSplatter (garden, no LOD) | M4 Air | — | 5.8 M | about 64 ms |
| AirVis | M2 Air | — | 100 M (a town) | not reported |

Grace Cathedral budgets 3.5 M splats on desktop and 1.4 M on mobile.

No M2 measurement exists. My extrapolation is about 6–15 ms for a 1–3 M budget at MetalFX internal resolution, before throttling and before the mesh forest is drawn.

Streaming splats at trail length is available only outside the recommended runtime.

- **PlayCanvas:** Streamed SOG with a global splat budget, WebGPU compute sorting, collision and relighting.
- **Spark 2.2.0:** streams LoD, but only on WebGL2.
- **CesiumJS:** streams splat LOD as 3D Tiles (April 2026).
- **three.js r186:** its splats have no LOD.
- **Godot GDGS 3.3.0:** no LOD. It targets Forward+ compute, and its Raster backend is beta. Its only Mac report (issue #2, closed March 2026) showed Metal shader-compile failures.
- **RealityKit:** renders splats natively on macOS 27, but it is not the planned engine.

Trail-scale capture would push the runtime to PlayCanvas and roughly double the agent build.

Training hero spots on the Mac became practical in 2026.

- **splatx-metal** (Apache-2.0, native Metal, with a thermal governor): trains the Mip-NeRF garden scene to 26.78 dB at a 2 M cap in 65.7 min on an M4 with 24 GB.
- **AirVis Studio:** free and local, and takes 360 video. It masks people, and needs macOS 26 or later, 16 GB of memory and 100 GB of project space.
- **Trail scale still needs CUDA:** BlitzGS trains city-scale aerial scenes in under 40 min on four A6000s. Structure-from-motion on about 260k frames comes on top of that.

Trail length, measured on the repo's OSM layer (ODbL):

- **Window measured:** the 5 × 5 km window with the most Jōgan lava-flow cover, 91%. It is the box x −3735 to 1265, z −1804 to 3196 in the repo's AEQD coordinates.
- **Paths in the window:** 39.9 km of path-type ways. Only about 9 km is named: 6.8 km of 'Fujishōji sen' (probably the Shōji route) and 2.0 km of the Tokai Nature Trail. The other 31 km is unnamed, and 1.2 km is tagged access=no.
- **Visitor routes:** the Fugaku–Narusawa nature trail is 1.4 km, the Saiko Nature Centre route about 2 km, and the AllTrails caves loop 9.3 km.
- **Share of the plot:** a ±10 m corridor along about 10 km of trail is 0.2 km², or 0.8% of the plot. All 40 km would be 3.2%.

My estimate of the capture effort for about 10 km of official trail:

- **Walking:** two passes at 0.5–0.7 m/s is 8–11 h of 360 video.
- **Storage:** the Insta360 X6 records 8K at up to 240 Mbps, about 108 GB/h, so 0.9–1.2 TB of raw video.
- **Frames:** at hierarchical-3DGS density (about 13 images per metre), about 260k.
- **Matching the planned fixed sun (25–35° elevation):** only about 1 h per clear day in mid-October (14:00–14:30 JST, azimuth 226–233°). That is about 1 km of trail a day, so 10 or more clear days.
- **Overcast capture:** removes the time limit but also loses the real sunflecks.
- **Insta360 Spatial Capture** (free, US from 28 September 2026): 2-minute clips, 4 scenes a month, processed by a Shenzhen vendor. It suits a test spot, not a trail.

Rules for capturing in the forest, read via search snippets because the hosts are blocked. They clarify the earlier claim that filming is forbidden.

- **Leaving the paths:** Japan's National Film Archive location database says it breaches the Natural Parks Act and the Cultural Properties Act.
- **Private use:** photos and video need no permit, but shooting off the path is not allowed and tripods are restricted.
- **Commercial posting** (YouTube, social media): needs an application through the Yamanashi Film Commission.
- **Sensitive shoots:** Yamanashi refuses shoots that could encourage suicide.
- **Prefectural visitor rules:** stay on marked trails.
- **Drones:** the Ministry of the Environment's Kanto office says no Natural Parks Act permit is needed, but the land manager's consent is. Yamanashi flies drone night patrols for suicide prevention. A drone sees nothing under the canopy.
- **Travel:** UK passport holders can visit visa-free, so a trip is possible.

The MMS road data is colour-true but not photographic near the camera.

- **The data:** the 2024 Yamanashi MMS has about 3 cm point spacing and real per-point camera RGB, at about 698 MB per 300 × 400 m sheet.
- **Consistency:** the catalogue warns that runs from different dates are not harmonised.
- **No images:** the release lists point clouds, orthophotos and micro-relief maps but no MMS images, so no radiance field can be trained from it.
- **On screen:** as point splats in a 1470-px, 90° view, 3 cm spacing is about 4–5 px at 5 m. It shrinks to 1 px only beyond about 22 m.
- **Known artefact:** colourised mobile scans paint sky colour onto edges and trees.
- **Coverage:** the best window has 15.9 km of road, including 6.0 km of Route 139. Actual MMS coverage there is unknown.

Photogrammetry is the kind of capture that blends with the lit world.

- **Apple Object Capture area mode:** runs on any Apple-silicon Mac and handles 'uneven terrain outdoors' and 2.5D surfaces. It can capture lava, moss and roots from the trail edge; once delit, these become relightable PBR assets.
- **Triangle Splatting+ and MeshSplatting:** export game-engine meshes that receive shadows, with walkable Unity demos. But they train on CUDA 12.6, bake the capture light into RGB-only colours, and lose about 2 dB PSNR.
- **Generative worlds:** Marble (US$20–95 a month) and Project Genie (US-only, 720p, about a minute of memory) look photoreal but are not this place.

what_it_would_take: Decide the target first: the current gate measures the UE5.8 look, not photorealism. Re-base it on calibrated real photos: a known camera, raw or bracketed exposures and a grey card, taken at the gate cameras' positions.

A £0–600 pilot before any trip: capture a mossy UK woodland on public paths with a 360 camera (X5 or X6) and train it locally with AirVis Studio or splatx-metal. Judge the look and the frame time on the owner's M2 in PlayCanvas.

A 7–10-day trip:
- Contact the Yamanashi Film Commission first.
- Stay on the trails, use no tripod, capture no people, and be sensitive to the forest's associations.
- Take two 2 TB external SSDs.
- Capture 10–15 hero spots plus about 10 km of official trail, in two passes.
- A sun-matched capture needs 10 or more clear days, because the light matches for only about 1 h a day. An overcast capture needs fewer days.

Photogrammetry with Object Capture area mode for lava, moss and root assets, plus bark and needle textures for the species trees. This is the part of capture that lifts the free-roam world, because the engine can light it.
MMS: measure its coverage from mmstrj.zip on the Mac. Use it only as a colour reference for road edges and as a distant backdrop, not as a walkable photoreal corridor.
unknowns: No splat frame time has been measured on any 8-core M2, whether in PlayCanvas, Spark, RealityKit or GDGS, and none alongside a mesh forest under fanless throttling.
Whether GDGS 3.3.0's compute or Raster backend now runs on Godot's Metal driver. Also whether the owner's Air will run macOS 27, which RealityKit splats need.
Forest-specific data on how quality falls off the capture path; only street-scene figures were found.

MMS coverage inside the plot (from mmstrj.zip), and whether the MMS camera images could be licensed from anyone.
The cost of cloud GPUs for training at trail scale; GPU price sites are blocked.
Whether the Insta360 X6 records 10-bit log or HDR well enough for the dynamic range under the canopy. Also whether JESTA will apply to UK visitors at trip time.
